title: Cascade Ortho Rider Certificate — Case Benefit Payment Clauses
content:
**How the Orthodontic Benefit Riders pay a case benefit: initial payment, installments and payees.**

## Clauses in force

1. **Initial payment.** For a new-start case, the initial payment is issued at banding. It is the rider's initial payment percentage of the case benefit, rounded half up to the cent. A case whose planned treatment months do not exceed the rider's lump-sum limit is instead paid in full as the initial payment.
2. **Installments.** The rest of the case benefit is paid in equal installments, one per service period at the rider's installment frequency (one month or one quarter). They are paid over the planned treatment months after the banding month, limited to the rider's installment months cap.
   - The number of installments is that number of months divided by the period length, rounded up.
   - Each installment is the remainder divided by the number of installments, rounded half up to the cent, and the last installment absorbs the rounding difference.
3. **First service period.** The first installment's service period begins the rider's first-installment offset in months after the banding month (after the establishment month for a takeover). Each later service period begins one period after the previous one.
4. **Payee.** Payments for in-network cases go to the practice, and payments for out-of-network cases go to the member.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following two clauses are **no longer in force** and have been superseded by the current basis for the case benefit and for the takeover proration:

- *Retired:* "The case benefit is the allowed case fee minus any unused lifetime orthodontic deductible, times the rider coinsurance for the case network (in network or out of network), rounded half up to the cent, and limited to the person's remaining lifetime maximum on the establishment date."
- *Retired:* "For a takeover case the benefit so computed is prorated by the months remaining divided by the planned treatment months (rounded half up to the cent) and is paid in installments only, with no initial payment."

## Worked split (hypothetical inputs)

Take a new-start case with a case benefit of 1,317.00 on a rider with a 30 percent initial payment, monthly installments, a 24-month cap and a 21-month plan.

- Initial payment: 30 percent of 1,317.00 is 395.10.
- Remainder: 1,317.00 less 395.10 is 921.90.
- Months after the banding month: 20, which is under the cap, so 20 monthly installments.
- Each installment: 921.90 divided by 20 is 46.095, which rounds to 46.10. The first 19 installments are 46.10 each (875.90 in total), and the last installment absorbs the rounding difference and is 46.00.

A 5-month plan on the same rider is within a 6-month lump-sum limit, so the whole case benefit would be the initial payment.

superseded_clauses: For a takeover case the benefit so computed is prorated by months_remaining divided by treatment_months (rounded half up to the cent) and is paid in installments only, with no initial payment.

The case benefit is the allowed_case_fee minus any unused ortho_lifetime_deductible, times the rider coinsurance for the case network (ortho_coinsurance_in_network or ortho_coinsurance_oon), rounded half up to the cent, and limited to the person's remaining lifetime maximum on the establishment date.
